items.prompt_text:
Write a Python regular expression that matches an ISO calendar date YYYY-MM-DD: any four-digit year, a month from 01 to 12 and a day from 01 to 31, separated by hyphens, with nothing before or after. Do not check days per month (2023-02-31 counts as valid).

It will be tested with re.fullmatch (so anchors are optional) against held-out strings: it must match every valid string and reject every invalid one. Examples (shown as JSON strings):

Must match:
  "1905-05-19"
  "2498-02-31"
  "2505-03-27"
  "0000-06-15"

Must not match:
  "1511-20-05"
  "1511-07-00"
  "1511-04-40"
  "1511-00-10"

Reply with only the pattern in a ```regex fenced block.
